text:
alex: Heads up — PR #18402 caused a CI microbench threshold fail on the batch-scheduler heatmap test. This is blocking the rollout.

maria: ugh. which metric popped?

alex: median batch_wait +14% and 95th tail latency +60ms on the smallbench-kv-fanout test. heatmap looks like a dense stripe in the 8-12ms bucket post-merge.

raj: any suspects? kernel selector change or prefetch sampler tweak?

alex: my eyeball on the flamegraph points to the new batch window estimator added in the merge — more frequent fanout into the kernel hotpath.

kelsey: CI logs + perf snippet:
```
smallbench-kv-fanout: baseline median 3.8ms -> HEAD 4.3ms (+13%).
95th: baseline 72ms -> HEAD 132ms (+83ms).
command: ./run_microbench --test kv-fanout --iters 500
```

ci-bot: test failure summary attached: https://ci.internal/runs/987654 -- threshold_diff: 0.032 (fail) :rotating_light:

maria: can we bisect to the commit? what's the merge range for #18402?

alex: merge touched these commits: 0a1b2c3..f9e8d7a. quick bisect plan:
```
git checkout main
git bisect start HEAD 0a1b2c3
# run ./tools/ci_microbench.sh smallbench-kv-fanout
```

raj: i'll kick off a bisect job on a small pool (won't affect production infra). if it points to the estimator change we can revert the single function. also will run with KV shadowing disabled to rule out cache interactions.

kelsey: attaching flamegraph snippet from the failing run: https://perf.artifacts/fg/1776543211.svg — shows `batch_window_estimator::compute` accounting for an extra 9% CPU and spawning more kernel dispatch.

maria: good call to shadow. if disabling shadowing removes the spike then it's a traffic pattern interaction with KV warmup.

alex: temporary mitigation: hold the canary rollout and block merge queue for that author until we confirm. pinging @oncall to pause automated rollouts.

ci-bot: rollout paused by ops-bot at 1776543300 (action: pause-canary).

raj: bisect job queued (job id 5721). will post results here.

kelsey: also adding a short test to the microbench to measure batch size distribution, will open a tiny PR to add it so CI gives more signal.

alex: thanks. once bisect identifies the culprit we should decide revert vs patch. prefer minimal revert that preserves other perf wins. :eyes:

ci-bot: bisect started, ETA ~25m. logs will stream here.

raj: first pass looks like commit f1e2d3a triggers the regression consistently. that commit is the estimator tweak.

maria: ok can someone draft a revert PR and opt into a follow-up that fixes the estimator? I'll coordinate codeowner review.

kelsey: created revert PR: #18415. linking microbench diff and flamegraph in the PR description.

alex: great. once CI on the revert is green, let's unpause canary and monitor the heatmap metric for a couple of hours.

ci-bot: revert PR #18415 CI passed on run 987712, canary unpause recommended.

maria: unpausing rollout now. tagging monitoring for 2h elevated watch. :rocket:

alex: postmortem note: add a perf unit test for batch size distribution and a guard that prevents estimator changes without a microbench pass. will file follow-ups.

raj: adding note: also add a KV-shadowed CI job to catch traffic-interaction regressions earlier.

kelsey: thanks team — good triage, quick bisect -> revert flow.
